item.title: New Source Layer — AI Transparency after August 2, 2026
item.lead: The legal context has changed since the previous edition: the European Commission published final guidelines on Article 50 AI Act on July 20, 2026; the transparency obligations apply from August 2, 2026.

blocks.text: The guidelines are directly relevant to the case because they clarify the distinction between systems that allow people to interact directly with AI and other forms of AI-generated or manipulated content. The relevant research question is not simply "was AI used?", but: which actor is the provider or deployer under the regulation, what type of system is being used, and what transparency action is required?

Therefore, the old phrasing "the human-in-the-loop is always exempt" must be avoided. A human operator who reviews AI output does not automatically equate every interaction legally to fully human communication. The factual role of the AI system and the applicable category must be determined on the basis of the regulation and the guidelines.

For the case, a concrete evidence protocol emerges: save model version, prompt/settings, generation output, human edits, sending time, and identity of the sender. Only then can it be determined afterwards which part of the interaction was human, AI-assisted, or fully automated.

blocks.label: SOURCE CHECK
blocks.text: The Commission states that Article 50 transparency obligations apply from August 2, 2026, and has published guidelines for this.
